A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a MEMS based parametric super regenerative receiver that uses 33 times less power than the previous MEMS based super regeneration work [1] and is 20 times faster than the fastest MEMS based parametic super regenerative receiver reported in literature [2].

the use of a parametric oscillator start-up principle for MEMS super-regenerative receivers can be applied to achieve a 33 times reduction in power consumption compared to the previous published mark.
we have developed a MEMS-based super regenerative receiver that is capable of receiving OOK signals at 1 GHz with sensitivity better than -67 dBm using just 15 \mu$W of RF pump power.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sustaining amplifier is not required to start the oscillator and can be replaced by an oscillator with lower power requirements.
the parametric oscillator pump power is the dominant power source, and that the RF front end power consumption is negligible.
the use of parametric principles in a MEMS based receiver front end is a viable alternative to conventional sustaining amplifier based front ends.
